chunks: From him, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman may incur debt on behalf of her husband while he is absent, so he shall pay off for her whatever she incurred in a reasonable manner.'

key_terms.بِالْمَعْرُوفِ: in a reasonable/fair manner / according to custom
key_terms.عَلَى زَوْجِهَا: on behalf of her husband / for her husband's account

ai.seo_question: What is the husband's financial responsibility for debts incurred by his wife while he is away?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of vicarious liability in marital finance, where a wife’s necessary expenditures during her husband’s absence bind him to repayment. The qualifier 'bil-ma'ruf' reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on proportionality and fairness, ensuring the debt aligns with customary standards rather than arbitrary amounts. This ruling underscores the husband’s role as the primary provider while protecting the wife’s right to manage household needs in his stead.
